title: review: T2: daemon re-respawns a queued unassigned review after respawn_after_s, counts respawns and holds with respawn_exhausted at [daemon].respawn_max
spec:
What: let the review respawn path retry instead of giving up after one attempt, with a visible cap.
Why: daemon.dispatch's respawn block (orchestrator/daemon.py:922-962) stamps pipeline.respawned_at once and then skips the task forever via the check that respawned_at is newer than the last requeue. When that respawned worker dies before claiming (crash, killed process, formerly a render error) the review or spec_review stays queued with no worker and no reason (gotcha 2026-09-21: T-0686 and T-0712 stamped respawned_at, no worker, no error on the bus). T-0756 already turned render errors into holds; this task covers every other silent death.
1. In the respawn block (both the pre-lock filter around daemon.py:938 and the locked recheck around 957): treat a stamped respawn as still pending only while now - respawned_at < respawn_after (same [daemon].respawn_after_s value, default 120). Older stamps on a task that is still queued with assigned_to None are eligible again.
2. Track pipeline.respawn_count (int, incremented at every respawn under the lock; a missing key counts as 0). Read [daemon].respawn_max from pool.cfg (default 3). When respawn_count already equals or exceeds respawn_max, do not spawn; instead set status held, hold_reason "respawn_exhausted: <count> respawns without a claim", pop pipeline.respawned_at, and notify.notify once with the task id (same message shape as hold_failed).
3. Document respawn_max in .orchestrator/pool.toml [daemon] next to respawn_after_s with a one-line comment (default 3); keep respawn_after_s unchanged.
Keep tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_respawns_requeued_review_once (two dispatch calls within the window still spawn exactly once and keep the same stamp), test_respawn_skips_task_claimed_between_snapshot_and_lock, test_respawn_skips_stale_review, test_respawn_ignores_unrelated_pipeline_keys, test_dispatch_respawns_unclaimed_spec_review_after_delay and test_respawn_age_uses_task_events_not_global_page green. Use the existing test helpers in tests/test_daemon.py (self.task, self.workers, P.Pool) and adjust time via the existing patterns in that file (patch daemon.time.time or backdate pipeline stamps). No new dependencies.
acceptance: tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_respawns_review_again_after_window — a queued unassigned review whose pipeline.respawned_at is older than respawn_after_s is spawned again by daemon.dispatch(pool): spawn.run_worker called once more, respawned_at moved forward, pipeline.respawn_count == 2; a stamp younger than the window is left alone

tests/test_daemon.py::test_respawn_holds_after_respawn_max — with pipeline.respawn_count == 3 (default respawn_max) and a stale stamp, daemon.dispatch(pool) does not spawn, sets status held with hold_reason startswith 'respawn_exhausted', removes pipeline.respawned_at and notify is called once with the task id; with [daemon].respawn_max = 5 in pool.cfg the same task is respawned instead
tests/test_pool.py::test_daemon_respawn_max_documented — .orchestrator/pool.toml [daemon] contains respawn_max = 3 (tomllib parse) and it sits next to respawn_after_s

result.summary: Verified the committed diff (160f28c in wt/T-0757) against all acceptance criteria and ran the full test_daemon.py + test_pool.py suite (255 tests, all pass). The time-window gate only blocks a stamped-but-unclaimed respawn; a genuine worker death still clears pipeline.respawned_at via _requeue's clear_pipeline_keys, so real repeated deaths respawn immediately while still incrementing respawn_count toward the cap. respawn_max defaults to 3, is read from pool.cfg, holds the task with the correct hold_reason and single notify call, pops respawned_at on exhaustion, and is documented in pool.toml immediately after respawn_after_s as required.
